mappings.note: three tethered animals sweep sectors (C-7.3-LO-1), but the question asks for the area that CANNOT be grazed, so the triangle minus those sectors is also a composite
sector minus a right triangle whose apex is not the chord, so the leftover is not a segment; it is a sector-and-triangle composite, LO-3 not LO-2
explicitly asks for the minor segment and then the major segment of the same chord - the paired minor/major wording of LO-2
major sector plus (equilateral triangle minus minor sector): three pieces added and subtracted, the composite outcome
minor segment and corresponding major segment for a 60 degree chord; sector minus triangle, the LO-2 method
ring between two concentric circles restricted to a 320 degree wedge: a difference of two sectors, composite
sector area alone for a 60 degree angle; nothing is subtracted, so it stays at LO-1
equilateral triangle LESS three 60 degree sectors - the subtraction is what makes this LO-3, unlike the earlier item where the sectors themselves were the answer
semicircle less an equilateral triangle formed by two radii; bounded by two chords, so it is not a segment, and the chord-length part comes from the isosceles radii not from LO-2
square less four corner quadrants, solved backwards for r from the given leftover area; composite region inverted
circle less an inscribed rectangle, the rectangle's diagonal giving the diameter; circle-and-polygon composite
quadrant less an inscribed square; the square's diagonal is the quadrant radius, a polygon-and-sector composite
racing track = two straight strips plus two semicircular annuli; several pieces assembled, the composite outcome
four semicircles of different diameters added and subtracted; no angle is given anywhere, so it is composite area rather than sector area
the two flower beds ARE the segments cut off by the sides of the square at the centre O; the marking scheme is sector minus triangle, which is LO-2
sum of the lawn AND the flower beds, i.e. two sectors plus two triangles added together; the whole region is assembled, not a single segment, so LO-3 rather than LO-2
square minus a circle plus a semicircle plus two quadrants - four pieces of different kinds, the clearest composite in the chapter

proof that a PERIMETER equals r[tan + sec + pi*theta/180 - 1]: the pi*theta/180 term is the arc (LO-1) and the rest is the straight boundary, so the item is about what a perimeter with a circular part contains
two large semicircles less two small ones; pure add-and-subtract of circular pieces
two internally touching circles with their areas summed and centres separated; the combined-circles relation, matching the other sum-of-areas items
quadrant less inscribed square again, with OA = 20; same composite skill as its 15 cm twin and deliberately given the same code
asks for the area AND the perimeter of the same rectangle-minus-semicircle region - the one item in the chapter that demands both sides of the distinction explicitly
clock hands again, but the DISTANCE travelled by the tips, i.e. arc length, not area; deliberately a different code from the minute-hand area item, which went to C-7.3-LO-1
square with a semicircle on each side, the overlaps giving petals; assembled and subtracted circular pieces over a polygon
regular hexagon less six 120 degree sectors at its vertices; the polygon supplies the angle but the answer is the subtraction, so composite
